We switched to Eglinton Vet less than a year ago because it was closer to us, and since then, we have visited multiple times with our dog for various health concerns as well as her annual vaccines. We have been so happy with the care provided by the entire clinic.

We have seen multiple vets, and they have all been wonderful — kind, compassionate, knowledgeable, and patient (which we appreciate with a dog who is nervous at the vet). They work with us based on our financial abilities and we never feel like expensive tests are being pushed on us. During the winter, our dog had a short hospital stay (elsewhere) at an emergency vet, and the follow-up appointment at Eglinton Vet was seamless. The vet had already reviewed the notes from the hospital, did a thorough exam, and worked with us to create a plan for a next follow-up. We were later referred to a specialist for the same issue, and we really appreciated how quickly and seamlessly Eglinton Vet handled the referral.

I also want to take a moment to specifically acknowledge Dr. Cevallos, who we have seen the most for both medical concerns and yearly exams and vaccines. We always leave feeling so incredibly appreciative of how kind and patient she is with us. She is very knowledgeable, informative and is genuinely so caring. She goes above and beyond, and we always feel that our dog is in great hands with her.

The front desk staff is also wonderful — everyone is friendly and always greets you as soon as you walk in. A special shout-out to Cassandra, who always takes the time to give our dog the nicest compliments and makes us feel so special!

UPDATE (05/28/26):

I have now paid the invoice and finally received Boo’s results/recommendations in writing after specifically requesting them.

I expected much better communication, organization, transparency, and attention to detail.

Instead:
• I requested an invoice on May 25 if bloodwork had already been completed.
• Instead of receiving the invoice, I received a voicemail requesting payment because I had supposedly “approved” the bloodwork.
• The invoice itself is dated May 26 but was not emailed to me until May 27, after my public review had already been posted.
• My written questions requesting clarification were ignored while payment was still being pushed.
• Yet once payment became involved, responses, confirmations, apologies, and documentation suddenly became immediate.
• Even in the final written medical explanation, Boo was referred to as “her” despite his file clearly stating he is male.

—————————

I genuinely hate leaving negative reviews, especially for places that are supposed to be caring, but this situation has left me feeling incredibly uncomfortable, stressed, and honestly a little taken advantage of during an already difficult time financially.

I took my dog Boo in for his yearly wellness exam and, trying to be honest and responsible, I voluntarily explained to the vet that I had temporarily stopped his flea/tick prevention because I had been out of work for some time and simply could not afford it. That was not easy for me to admit, but I wanted to be upfront because Boo’s health matters to me deeply.

The vet seemed understanding during the appointment, examined Boo, and told me he otherwise looked healthy. The only thing left was his 4DX test.

A few days later, I then received a phone call from a completely different vet, someone who hadn’t examined Boo, saying the original vet had left a note on his desk stating Boo tested positive for Lyme exposure and should have additional bloodwork and a urine test done. During that call, I was told the total would be $170 + tax.

Shortly after, I then received an email saying the price was actually $177 + tax instead. Since the pricing changed, I politely replied asking for clarification because I was already stressed about whether I could even afford the testing in the first place.

Nobody responded.

Instead, after I explained by email that I could not afford both tests and asked them to let me know if any bloodwork had already been completed so I could review the invoice and arrange payment, I then received another phone call the following day (Tuesday, May 26, 2026) around 4:15PM telling me I owed $186 for bloodwork because I had “approved” it.

What upset me most is that I never received an invoice specifically for the bloodwork beforehand, never received written clarification regarding the changing prices, and never once said “go ahead and charge me without sending documentation.” I specifically said that IF testing had already been completed, I would absolutely pay once I received the invoice for it.

As someone who had already explained they were struggling financially, the entire situation honestly made me feel pressured, dismissed, and extremely anxious. I was trying to ask questions, understand the costs, and be responsible, not avoid payment.

I genuinely do not think it is unreasonable to expect a proper invoice before being repeatedly asked for money, especially when the pricing changed more than once and written clarification was ignored.

As of writing this review (Tuesday, May 26, 2026 at 5:08 PM EST), I am STILL waiting for this $186 invoice to arrive in my inbox, so it would honestly be quite the “coincidence” if the invoice suddenly appeared only after this review was posted.

I love my dog deeply and would never intentionally neglect his care. Financial hardship can happen to anyone, and being honest about that should not leave someone feeling confused, pressured, or embarrassed afterward.

Overall, the experience felt financially unclear, poorly communicated, and emotionally stressful at a time when I was already vulnerable.

contacted Eglinton Veterinary Facilities to book an appointment for my dog, Teddy, specifically for a small rash on his belly and to refill medication already in his veterinary history.
When booking the appointment, I clearly explained the reason for the visit. However, I was surprised at checkout to receive a bill of $268.95, including a $122 consultation fee, Isaderm 15 g for $75, and Cefaseptin 300 mg for $41.04.
After returning home, I checked the approximate retail price of Isaderm cream online in Canada and found prices generally ranging between $26 and $42 CAD, which made the charge even more surprising.
I understand veterinary care is expensive, however, for such a specific and limited concern, I was not expecting a total cost close to $270.
Unfortunately, this was my second disappointing experience, which is why I felt it was important to share this feedback.
